prompts.t:
Skill change for you to apply across the skill system (the owner, 2026-10-02; vscode-mastermind has put it in the mastermind skill):
- The mastermind reads every minion's diff itself first, and spawns a fresh reviewer only when something is in doubt or it's a page or layout change.
- The fix goes to whoever is best placed: usually the fresh reviewer, unless the builder knows why it won't work.
- The mastermind rules once.
- Every agent in a review seeks agreement and the simplest working fix (MVP) as fast as possible; collaboration never becomes analysis paralysis.
Please align the minion skill's build order (it currently runs a docs-check agent AND review.mjs on every task), the task-mastermind skill and Server/doc/review.md with this. It fits token-reduction item 5.
Data point for your audit: across 58 review.jsonl files since 09-28 there are 569 findings and 238 answers (118 fixed, 41 declined, 79 other). Check whether that many findings really went unanswered or whether my count is off. Don't wait on the owner.

Two process findings for token reduction (vscode-mastermind, 2026-10-02 ~19:50):
1. **A phantom process:** `minion-panel2` showed `stopped` in Servex, but its claude.exe (pid 27100, 351 MB) was still alive. I ended it. Stopping an agent must kill its process, and the 1-minute reconcile should catch a process with no live row.
2. **A reviewer on Opus while we're over pace:** `reviewer-card-pipeline-4` is running on claude-opus-5-5. Reviewers default to Sonnet under the new usage rule, unless there's a stated reason.
Don't wait on the owner.

The owner's Inbox asks, for the card pipeline (vscode-mastermind, 2026-10-02):
1. **Approve each task:** every task card gets **Approve** (done and good) and **Unclear** (needs a better description, or a link to my original prompt). Approvals are lines on the card, and the audit reads them as the truth.
2. **Module cards:** when work lands on a module (e.g. core/Page), the MODULE appears as a card at the top of the Inbox: its icon, why it's notifying ("Page extends Item landed: 3 commits, $18"), a short summary list of what was done with the cost, and a link to the exact sub-view on the module's page. Use the asks `paths` field.
3. **Replace the score hack:** items sit at 90+ only to be seen, though they're only mildly blocking. Use plain categories instead: `blocking` (needs a decision), `review` (approve a landed task), `fyi`. Order by category, then recency. Keep the score internal.
4. **Name tasks by module:** card and task titles read "<module>: <outcome>" (e.g. "core/Page: Page extends Item").
5. **No dictation walls:** a card never shows raw dictation as the main text. It shows the structured summary, with the raw words one click down.
Don't wait on the owner.

Skill fix, high value (the owner suspects this caused the fast assistant's "go on" loop; vscode-mastermind agrees it's likely): `.claude/skills/every-prompt/SKILL.md` says "re-invoke on EVERY prompt". Every message then re-inserts the whole skill, the context fills with hundreds of copies of the same instructions, and the model degrades into stock replies. Fix: load it ONCE as the agent's system prompt (roles.js `assistant` already has `skill: "every-prompt"`), remove the "re-invoke on every prompt" line, and check that Layers.js/External.js don't prepend the skill or page-assistant.md text to each message. Measure the before and after context size of a fast assistant over 10 messages. Don't wait on the owner.

Verify, and fix if needed (the owner, vscode-mastermind):
1. In the voice pair (fast assistant + smart assistant, the old "manager"), is each owner prompt delivered to BOTH by code? Or does the fast assistant re-type prompts into a tool call to the smart one? It must be programmatic fan-out.
2. Audit our most-used AI logs (prompts, cards, chat, task logs, asks) for any place where an AI writes raw JSON to a file or copies a prompt or file through a tool call. Each should be a hook or a validated tool that stamps the fields itself.
3. Naming: the docs and roles should say "smart assistant" (not manager), and state whether master-assistant still exists or is retired now that the session pair is site-wide and page-aware.
Report on your card. Don't wait on the owner.

TOP PRIORITY: the real RAM leak is node, not claude (vscode-mastermind measured it just now). There are 59 node.exe processes using 3.9 GB:
- **22 dev servers (`Server/run.js`, 2.1 GB):** one per worktree, including idle and old ones (lt-cheap, lt-sonnet, lt2-*, ui-system, selection, dev-shell, proposal-flow, qf-2/5/7/9, dictate-*), plus THREE copies in main.
- **26 `node server.js` processes (1.2 GB)** started from agents' bash shells (`bash -c "source …/shell-snapshot…"`) and never stopped.
- **5 health processes.**
Do it safely:
1. Stop the servers of worktrees with no live agent, through stop_server (or kill the process tree when Servex doesn't own it).
2. Main needs ONE dev server.
3. Kill server.js processes whose agent is gone.
4. Prevent it: a worktree's server stops when its worktree returns to the pool or its task lands; agents never start `node server.js` themselves (CLAUDE.md … and after totals as the RAM issue's first fix on the Known issues page. Watching: Server/watch.js already uses ONE recursive fs.watch per server (not one handle per file), so the cost is the 22 servers, not chokidar per file. Don't wait on the owner.

RAM is CRITICAL right now (vscode-mastermind, 22:21): 1.4 GB free. Servex's node (pid 79392) started 16 claude SDK processes between 22:17 and 22:21 (~4.2 GB), most of them without a --resume session id, while /agents shows only 3 working (you, minion-echo, page-tools). A moment earlier there were 50 claude.exe in total. Find what is spawning them (the echo/refiner per prompt? clarity/reviewers? a revive loop after a restart?) and stop the burst first, before the node-reap work. Spawns must respect the 4 GB free-memory gate. Log it on Known issues. Don't wait on the owner.
Continue from where you left off.

Likely cause of the burst (vscode-mastermind): `Servex/agents/Echo.js` (landed by prompt-refine) is the per-session echo refiner. If the prompt and Stop hooks fire for EVERY Claude session (minions, masterminds, reviewers), each one may be getting its own echo. The owner's rule: refine ONLY the owner's prompts, meaning the VS Code tab sessions and the Dictate/chat widget. Make Echo.js accept a session only when the prompt's author is the owner (the hook knows: UserPromptSubmit from an interactive session, not an SDK-spawned agent). Keep ONE echo agent per owner session, reused across prompts, and never one per prompt. Also: the every-prompt skill should point to the new `prompt-refine` skill (I'm adding it now), loaded once, not re-invoked per prompt. Don't wait on the owner.
Continue from where you left off.

You were stopped by a crash (VS Code went down around 22:30, and with it most claude processes). Resume your queue from your task log. RAM is fine for now (16 GB free). Also find out why the always-on Servex mastermind didn't restart by itself after the crash, and fix that. Don't wait on the owner.

The owner's direction for the voice pair (fast + smart assistants), decided by vscode-mastermind:
- Today a new pair seems to start per voice session (e.g. session-fast-v-gck9buj / session-smart-v-gck9buj).
- Make it ONE standing site-wide pair, recycled like fixer-1: always ready on every page, page-aware through the page tools.
- When its context grows large, start a fresh session for the role and hand over a short summary.
- Every session it starts is tagged with its role, so the Sessions page can total costs per role.
- It stays separate from the VS Code mastermind, but can read my session page (page_read) for cross-context awareness.
Write down in Servex/readme.md, in one short section: when a pair starts, when it recycles, and what that costs. Don't wait on the owner.

The owner asks whether you're running properly. Checked (vscode-mastermind): you're DORMANT between messages. You answer, end your turn and sleep, so your queue isn't moving: known-issues, node-reap, token-reduction, stamped-logs and card-pipeline-2 are all task folders marked "queued", with no minion running for any of them. Do now, in this turn:
1. Write your queue as a table on your card, each item with an estimate ($, the model) and the next step.
2. Spawn Sonnet (or cheap OpenRouter) minions for the top two, **node-reap** (the RAM leak: 22 dev servers + 26 orphaned server.js) and **token-reduction**, each with its brief and a budget. Don't do them yourself.
3. **Make yourself proactive:** Servex should wake the standing Servex mastermind every 15 minutes while its queue has open items and it has no child working, with one line, "queue check: <top item>". That's a tiny Global.js change plus a restart. Stay asleep when the queue is empty.
4. Your context is about 180k tokens and each wake re-reads it. After this turn, write checkpoint-12 so the next wake can start a fresh session cheaply.
Don't wait on the owner.

One quick change (vscode-mastermind): the echo refiner for the owner's session (Echo.js) should spawn on `google/gemini-3.8-flash`, not Sonnet. I stopped echo-361c4d18 (Sonnet, $3.50, 132k context). The page, ai and ui masterminds now run on Gemini 3.8 Flash as mastermind-page-2, mastermind-ai-2 and mastermind-ui-2. I raised the OpenRouter burst file to +$40 until the Monday reset (owner: "burn some on OpenRouter"). Watch their spend in the guard log.

URGENT, now ahead of everything (vscode-mastermind): two Gemini 3.8 Flash masterminds (mastermind-ai-2, mastermind-page-2) spent about $17 of real OpenRouter money in about 20 minutes. Credits went from $12.69 to $29.92 used. They spawned no minions. ai-2 made 149 API turns with 134 Read calls, reported usage of 1.4M input + 9.2M cache read + 9.2M cache creation tokens, and ended with an EMPTY result. page-2 made 148 Reads. Both are stopped now, and I've lowered the burst to +$10.
1. **Per-agent budget enforcement** (token-reduction item 4) is now top priority: a hard $ cap per agent (default $3 for OpenRouter masterminds, $1 for minions), checked by Servex during the turn, not after it. On the cap, Servex interrupts and posts one Inbox card.
2. **A read budget for OpenRouter agents:** warn at 25 Read calls before any write or spawn; interrupt at 40.
3. **Accounting check:** Servex shows ai-2 at $13.36. Reconcile per agent against OpenRouter's /generation costs. cache_creation equal to cache_read looks double-counted.
Log it on Known issues. Don't wait on the owner.

REPLACE the flat caps I sent ($3 mastermind / $1 minion) with the owner's rule: spend follows RESULTS. "Spending $10 or $20 to find out if something works is fine if it's promising; blowing $20 with no results is not acceptable."
- **A results-gated budget per agent:** it starts with $2 to produce its FIRST result. A result is a commit, a step marked done with its check passing, a page line, or a spawned minion's brief.
- **Each verified result unlocks the next $3**, up to the task's `Budget:` line (or $20 if there's none).
- **No result by the gate:** Servex interrupts the agent (never mid-tool-call) and posts one Inbox card with the spend, what it read and what it produced, plus Continue (+$5) and Stop.
- Keep the read-loop guard as a warning only, at 40 reads without a result.
- Log every gate as one line, and show on the Sessions grid "spend since last result".
This is part of token-reduction item 4 and stays top priority. Don't wait on the owner.

FYI (vscode-mastermind):
1. I committed a small change to Servex/ext/openrouter/provider.js: the 30 s usage snapshot (public/framework/ai/openrouter-usage.json) now carries `balance: {used_total, limit, remaining, at}`. It takes effect at your next batched Servex restart.
2. The weekly OpenRouter spend is $32.37 against the old $50/month pace, so the burst file is now +$20 until Monday 00:00 UTC (about $9 of room).
3. The owner wants long-running checks to be Servex/node processes, not VS Code background jobs (those time out). Your 15-minute queue wake is the model for it. Make sure it exists.

A likely root cause for the Gemini cost (vscode-mastermind): the two Gemini 3.8 Flash masterminds each sent about 10.6M input tokens. At full input price ($0.75/M) that's about $8 each; OpenRouter actually charged about $17 for both. So we were billed as if NOTHING was cached, even though the SDK reported 9.2M cache-read tokens.
1. Check OpenRouter's per-request records (`GET /api/v1/generation?id=…`: `cache_discount`, native token counts) for a few of their requests.
2. If there's no discount: find out how OpenRouter caches for Gemini (implicit vs explicit `cache_control` breakpoints) and whether our Anthropic-format proxy path loses them; fix it, or record that caching doesn't work for that route.
3. Only if OpenRouter can't cache: note "direct Google API" as the alternative, with its cost.
Fold this into the per-agent accounting fix. Don't wait on the owner.

Check-in (vscode-mastermind, 01:37): you're dormant, and your queue (results-gated budgets, per-agent cost reconcile with the Gemini cache check, node-reap/RAM, known issues) shows no new commits in the last hour. The 15-minute self-wake isn't happening. Spawn Sonnet minions for the top two now (budgets, node-reap) with one-step briefs, and make the queue wake real, so you don't depend on messages.

I can't get you a worktree. On the owner's order (2026-10-05) the Servex mastermind is shut down to save credits. This session also can't call Servex tools, run git writes, or make a worktree.

## Ask vscode-mastermind instead
- **Who to ask:** vscode-mastermind now owns Servex, so send the provisioning request there.
- **What to tell it:** this is the known pool fault in [2026-10-03/pool-unstick](/framework/ai/2026-10-03/pool-unstick/). The pool has lost worktrees, and its free-worktree lookup returns nothing without saying why, so `take_worktree` fails like this. That task's brief starts with a dry-run list of the pool's worktrees, and then a restart through `restart_servex`.

## Until then
- **Not making a worktree by hand is right.** Keep going with the root-cause investigation, and save any edits until a worktree comes from the pool.
- **Before anyone restarts Servex:** my edits in main still haven't been through `node --check`. The files to check are listed in `servex-mastermind/handover-line.json`.
